import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Read the data
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')

# Create a figure with multiple subplots
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 12))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 3, hspace=0.3, wspace=0.3)

# 1. Income distribution by Education
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
education_order = df.groupby('Education')['Income'].median().sort_values(ascending=False).index
sns.boxplot(data=df, y='Education', x='Income', order=education_order, ax=ax1, palette='viridis')
ax1.set_title('Income Distribution by Education Level', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_xlabel('Income')
ax1.set_ylabel('Education')

# 2. Age distribution
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 1])
current_year = 2014  # Based on the dates in the data
df['Age'] = current_year - df['Year_Birth']
ax2.hist(df['Age'], bins=20, color='steelblue', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax2.set_title('Age Distribution of Customers', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_xlabel('Age')
ax2.set_ylabel('Frequency')
ax2.grid(alpha=0.3)

# 3. Spending by category
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 2])
spending_cols = ['MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 'MntFishProducts', 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds']
spending_totals = df[spending_cols].sum()
colors = plt.cm.Set3(range(len(spending_cols)))
ax3.pie(spending_totals, labels=['Wines', 'Fruits', 'Meat', 'Fish', 'Sweets', 'Gold'], 
        autopct='%1.1f%%', colors=colors, startangle=90)
ax3.set_title('Total Spending by Product Category', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')

# 4. Marital Status distribution
ax4 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 0])
marital_counts = df['Marital_Status'].value_counts()
ax4.bar(marital_counts.index, marital_counts.values, color='coral', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax4.set_title('Distribution of Marital Status', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax4.set_xlabel('Marital Status')
ax4.set_ylabel('Count')
ax4.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
ax4.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)

# 5. Purchase channels comparison
ax5 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 1])
purchase_cols = ['NumWebPurchases', 'NumCatalogPurchases', 'NumStorePurchases']
purchase_means = df[purchase_cols].mean()
x_pos = np.arange(len(purchase_cols))
bars = ax5.bar(x_pos, purchase_means, color=['#FF6B6B', '#4ECDC4', '#45B7D1'], 
               edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax5.set_xticks(x_pos)
ax5.set_xticklabels(['Web', 'Catalog', 'Store'])
ax5.set_title('Average Purchases by Channel', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax5.set_ylabel('Average Number of Purchases')
ax5.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)

# 6. Income vs Total Spending
ax6 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 2])
df['TotalSpending'] = df[spending_cols].sum(axis=1)
scatter = ax6.scatter(df['Income'], df['TotalSpending'], c=df['Age'], 
                     cmap='coolwarm', alpha=0.6, edgecolors='black', linewidth=0.5)
ax6.set_title('Income vs Total Spending (colored by Age)', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax6.set_xlabel('Income')
ax6.set_ylabel('Total Spending')
ax6.grid(alpha=0.3)
cbar = plt.colorbar(scatter, ax=ax6)
cbar.set_label('Age')

# 7. Children at home distribution
ax7 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 0])
df['TotalKids'] = df['Kidhome'] + df['Teenhome']
kids_counts = df['TotalKids'].value_counts().sort_index()
ax7.bar(kids_counts.index, kids_counts.values, color='lightgreen', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax7.set_title('Distribution of Total Children at Home', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax7.set_xlabel('Number of Children')
ax7.set_ylabel('Count')
ax7.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)

# 8. Campaign acceptance rates
ax8 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 1])
campaign_cols = ['AcceptedCmp1', 'AcceptedCmp2', 'AcceptedCmp3', 'AcceptedCmp4', 'AcceptedCmp5', 'Response']
acceptance_rates = df[campaign_cols].mean() * 100
x_pos = np.arange(len(campaign_cols))
bars = ax8.bar(x_pos, acceptance_rates, color='mediumpurple', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax8.set_xticks(x_pos)
ax8.set_xticklabels(['Cmp1', 'Cmp2', 'Cmp3', 'Cmp4', 'Cmp5', 'Response'], rotation=45)
ax8.set_title('Campaign Acceptance Rates', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax8.set_ylabel('Acceptance Rate (%)')
ax8.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)

# 9. Recency vs Web Visits
ax9 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 2])
ax9.scatter(df['Recency'], df['NumWebVisitsMonth'], alpha=0.6, 
           color='orange', edgecolors='black', linewidth=0.5)
ax9.set_title('Recency vs Web Visits per Month', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax9.set_xlabel('Recency (days since last purchase)')
ax9.set_ylabel('Web Visits per Month')
ax9.grid(alpha=0.3)

# Add main title
fig.suptitle('Customer Marketing Campaign Analysis Dashboard', 
             fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=0.995)

plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()
